competitors.title: Announcing new Temporal capabilities from Replay 2026
key_points: Serverless Workers: auto-scaling workers for bursty AI workloads, pay-per-execution model
Standalone Activities: independent function execution without a full Workflow, ideal for lightweight AI functions
Workflow Streams: real-time streaming between Workflows and external consumers, enabling LLM token streaming through Temporal
External Payload Storage: offload large AI context payloads (prompts, embeddings) from Event History to reduce cost and avoid size limits
Google ADK integration: native integration with Google's Agent Development Kit for building agentic systems on Temporal
OpenAI Agents SDK integration: seamless handoff between Temporal Activities and OpenAI Agents SDK
AWS AI Competency: Temporal Cloud recognized as AWS AI Competency Partner
Worker Versioning: safe rollouts of AI agent behavior changes
Task Queue Priority & Fairness: prioritize critical AI agent tasks over background processing
Billing API, SCIM: enterprise governance for AI agent deployments

Self-hosted Temporal Server for data sovereignty requirements

competitors.title: Durable Player Sessions with Temporal Actor Workflows
key_points: Actor Workflow pattern: each entity (player/agent) gets their own durable, independently-addressable Workflow
AI agents are explicitly described as Actor Workflows: receive instructions (Signals/Updates), maintain conversational state, call external services (Activities)
Workflow holds state in memory durably — no database reads on recovery, no reconnection logic
Continue-As-New prevents unbounded history growth for sessions lasting weeks or months
Each actor is independently addressable by Workflow Id — any service can Signal, Query, or Update it
Search Attributes make active agents queryable by operators: state, duration, activity

competitors.title: Human-in-the-Loop Approval Workflows with Temporal
key_points: wait_condition() suspends Workflow execution durably — consumes zero compute while waiting for human response
Durable timers enforce SLA deadlines: automatic escalation when no response within window
Complete audit trail recorded at every step — decisions, reminders, escalations — survives infrastructure failure
Resubmission loops handled cleanly with Continue-As-New
Pattern directly applicable to AI agent guardrails: require human approval before high-stakes actions
40-80 events per approval cycle — well within Temporal's 50K event limit
Activities must be idempotent: same inputs produce same outcomes even when retried
